q: Find the square roots of the complex number \( z = 8i \).
c:
Solution

The trigonometric form of \( z = 8i \), with \( -\pi<\theta\le\pi \), is
\[z=8\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\]

The square roots are
\[w_k=\sqrt{8}\left(\cos\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{2}\right),\quad k=0,1\]

For \( k = 0 \):
\[w_0=2\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=2\sqrt{2}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(1+i)=2+2i\]

For \( k = 1 \):
\[w_1=2\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{4}\right)=-2-2i\]


Answer   \( \pm(2+2i) \)

q: Find the square roots of the complex number \( z = -18 \).
c:
Solution

\[z=18(\cos\pi+i\sin\pi)\]

\[w_k=\sqrt{18}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi+2k\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi+2k\pi}{2}\right),\quad k=0,1\]

\[k=0:\quad w_0=3\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=3\sqrt{2}\, i\]

\[k=1:\quad w_1=3\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)=-3\sqrt{2}\, i\]


Answer   \( \pm 3\sqrt{2}\, i \)

q: Find the square roots of the complex number \( z = -8 + 8\sqrt{3}\, i \).
c:
Solution

\[r=\sqrt{64+192}=16\]

\[\cos\theta=-\dfrac12,\quad\sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\implies\theta=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\]

\[w_k=4\left(\cos\dfrac{\frac{2\pi}{3}+2k\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\frac{2\pi}{3}+2k\pi}{2}\right),\quad k=0,1\]

\[k=0:\quad w_0=4\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)=2+2\sqrt{3}\, i\]

\[k=1:\quad w_1=4\left(\cos\dfrac{4\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)=-2-2\sqrt{3}\, i\]


Answer   \( \pm(2+2\sqrt{3}\, i) \)

q: Find the square roots of the complex number \( z = 4 + 4\sqrt{3}\, i \).
c:
Solution

\[r=\sqrt{16+48}=8\]

\[\cos\theta=\dfrac12,\quad\sin\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\implies\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}\]

\[w_k=2\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{3}+2k\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{3}+2k\pi}{2}\right),\quad k=0,1\]

\[k=0:\quad w_0=2\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}\, i\]

\[k=1:\quad w_1=2\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)=-\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}\, i\]


Answer   \( \pm(\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}\, i) \)

q: Find the square roots of the complex number \( z = -i \).
c:
Solution

With \( -\pi<\theta\le\pi \),
\[z=1\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)\]

(Do not use \( \theta=\dfrac{3\pi}{2} \).)
\[w_k=\cos\dfrac{-\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{-\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{2},\quad k=0,1\]

\[k=0:\quad w_0=\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}i\]

\[k=1:\quad w_1=\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{4}=-\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}+\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}i\]


Answer   \( \pm\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(1-i) \)

q: Find the square roots of the complex number \( z = -4\sqrt{3} - 4i \).
c:
Solution

\[r=\sqrt{48+16}=8\]

\[\cos\theta=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\quad\sin\theta=-\dfrac12\implies\theta=-\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\]

\[w_k=2\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{-\frac{5\pi}{6}+2k\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{-\frac{5\pi}{6}+2k\pi}{2}\right),\quad k=0,1\]

For \( k = 0 \), the argument is \( -\dfrac{5\pi}{12} \). Using
\[\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{12}=\dfrac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4},\quad\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{12}=\dfrac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}\]

\[\begin{aligned}w_0&=2\sqrt{2}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{6}-\sqrt{2}}{4}-\dfrac{\sqrt{6}+\sqrt{2}}{4}i\right)\\&=(\sqrt{3}-1)-(\sqrt{3}+1)i.\end{aligned}\]

For \( k = 1 \), \( w_1 = -w_0 \):
\[w_1=(1-\sqrt{3})+(1+\sqrt{3})i\]


Answer   \( (\sqrt{3}-1)-(\sqrt{3}+1)i,\; (1-\sqrt{3})+(1+\sqrt{3})i \)

q: Solve the equation \( z^3 = 8 \), where \( z \) is a complex number.
c:
Solution

\[8=8(\cos 0+i\sin 0)\]

\[z_k=2\left(\cos\dfrac{2k\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{2k\pi}{3}\right),\quad k=0,1,2\]

\[k=0:\quad z_0=2\]

\[k=1:\quad z_1=2\left(-\dfrac12+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right)=-1+\sqrt{3}\, i\]

\[k=2:\quad z_2=-1-\sqrt{3}\, i\]


Answer   \( 2,\; -1\pm\sqrt{3}\, i \)

q: Solve the equation \( z^3 = -8i \), where \( z \) is a complex number.
c:
Solution

With \( -\pi<\theta\le\pi \),
\[-8i=8\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)\]

\[z_k=2\left(\cos\dfrac{-\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{-\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{3}\right),\quad k=0,1,2\]

\[k=0:\quad z_0=2\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)=\sqrt{3}-i\]

\[k=1:\quad z_1=2\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=2i\]

\[k=2:\quad z_2=2\left(\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)=-\sqrt{3}-i\]


Answer   \( \sqrt{3}-i,\; 2i,\; -\sqrt{3}-i \)

q: Solve the equation \( z^3 = 27i \), where \( z \) is a complex number.
c:
Solution

\[27i=27\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\]

\[z_k=3\left(\cos\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{3}\right),\quad k=0,1,2\]

\[k=0:\quad z_0=3\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{3}{2}i\]

\[k=1:\quad z_1=3\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)=-\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{3}{2}i\]

\[k=2:\quad z_2=3\left(\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)=-3i\]


Answer   \( \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{3}{2}i,\; -\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{3}{2}i,\; -3i \)

q: Solve the equation \( z^3 = -i \), where \( z \) is a complex number.
c:
Solution

\[-i=\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\]

\[z_k=\cos\dfrac{-\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{-\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{3},\quad k=0,1,2\]

\[k=0:\quad z_0=\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac12 i\]

\[k=1:\quad z_1=\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}=i\]

\[k=2:\quad z_2=\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{6}=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac12 i\]


Answer   \( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac12 i,\; i,\; -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac12 i \)

q: Verify that \( z = 1 - 2i \) is a solution of the equation \( z^2 - 2z + 5 = 0 \).
c:
Solution

\[\begin{aligned}z^2&=(1-2i)^2=1-4i+4i^2=-3-4i,\\-2z&=-2+4i.\end{aligned}\]

\[z^2-2z+5=(-3-4i)+(-2+4i)+5=0.\]

The left-hand side equals the right-hand side, so \( z = 1 - 2i \) is a solution.

Answer   \( verified \)

q: Verify that \( z = -2 + i \) is a solution of the equation \( z^2 + 4z + 5 = 0 \).
c:
Solution

\[\begin{aligned}z^2&=(-2+i)^2=4-4i+i^2=3-4i,\\4z&=-8+4i.\end{aligned}\]

\[z^2+4z+5=(3-4i)+(-8+4i)+5=0.\]


Answer   \( verified \)

q: Verify that \( z = 2i \) is a solution of the equation \( z^2 + z + \bar{z} + 4 = 0 \).
c:
Solution

\[z^2=(2i)^2=-4,\qquad z+\bar{z}=2i+(-2i)=0\]

\[z^2+z+\bar{z}+4=-4+0+4=0\]


Answer   \( verified \)

q: Verify that \( z = 2 + i \) is a solution of the equation \( z^2 - 4z + 5 = 0 \).
c:
Solution

\[z^2=(2+i)^2=4+4i+i^2=3+4i\]

\[-4z=-8-4i\]

\[z^2-4z+5=(3+4i)+(-8-4i)+5=0\]


Answer   \( verified \)

q: Given \( z = -2\sqrt{3} + 2i \), find \( z^{-1} \) using trigonometric form and check that \( z\, z^{-1} = 1 \).
c:
Solution

\[r=\sqrt{12+4}=4\]

\[\cos\theta=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\quad\sin\theta=\dfrac12\implies\theta=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\]

\[z=4\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)\]

\[z^{-1}=\dfrac14\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)\right)=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{8}-\dfrac18 i\]

Check:
\[(-2\sqrt{3}+2i)\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{8}-\dfrac18 i\right)=\dfrac{6+2}{8}=1\]


Answer   \( -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{8}-\dfrac18 i \)

q: Given \( z = 3 - 3i \), find \( z^{-1} \) using trigonometric form and check that \( z\, z^{-1} = 1 \).
c:
Solution

\[r=3\sqrt{2},\qquad\theta=-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\]

\[z=3\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)\]

\[z^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\dfrac{1}{6}+\dfrac16 i\]

Check:
\[(3-3i)\left(\dfrac{1+i}{6}\right)=\dfrac{3+3i-3i-3i^2}{6}=1\]


Answer   \( \dfrac16+\dfrac16 i \)

q: Given \( z = -5i \), find \( z^{-1} \) using trigonometric form and check that \( z\, z^{-1} = 1 \).
c:
Solution

With \( -\pi<\theta\le\pi \),
\[z=5\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)\]

\[z^{-1}=\dfrac15\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=\dfrac15 i\]

Check: \( (-5i)\left(\dfrac{i}{5}\right)=-i^2=1 \).

Answer   \( \dfrac15 i \)

q: Given \( z = 2\sqrt{3} - 2i \), find \( \dfrac{z}{\bar{z}} \) using trigonometric forms.
c:
Solution

\[z=4\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\]

\[\bar{z}=4\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\]

\[\begin{aligned}\dfrac{z}{\bar{z}}&=\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)\\&=\dfrac12-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i.\end{aligned}\]


Answer   \( \dfrac12-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i \)

q: Given \( z = -1 + \sqrt{3}\, i \), find \( \dfrac{z}{\bar{z}} \) using trigonometric forms.
c:
Solution

\[z=2\left(\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)\]

\[\bar{z}=2\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right)\]

\[\dfrac{z}{\bar{z}}=\cos\dfrac{4\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{4\pi}{3}=-\dfrac12-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\]


Answer   \( -\dfrac12-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i \)

q: Given \( z = -2 - 2i \), find \( \dfrac{z}{\bar{z}} \) using trigonometric forms.
c:
Solution

\[z=2\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)\right)\]

\[\bar{z}=2\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right)\]

\[\dfrac{z}{\bar{z}}=\cos\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)=i\]


Answer   \( i \)

q: Evaluate \( (1 - i)^8 \) using De Moivre's theorem.
c:
Solution

\[1-i=\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)\]

\[\begin{aligned}(1-i)^8&=(\sqrt{2})^8\left(\cos(-2\pi)+i\sin(-2\pi)\right)\\&=16(1+0i)=16.\end{aligned}\]


Answer   \( 16 \)

q: Evaluate \( \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-i}{1+i}\right)^6 \) using De Moivre's theorem.
c:
Solution

\[\sqrt{3}-i=2\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)\]

\[1+i=\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\]

\[\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-i}{1+i}=\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{5\pi}{12}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{5\pi}{12}\right)\right)\]

\[\begin{aligned}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}-i}{1+i}\right)^6&=(\sqrt{2})^6\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{5\pi}{2}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{5\pi}{2}\right)\right)\\&=8\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)=-8i.\end{aligned}\]

Here \( -\dfrac{5\pi}{2}+2\pi=-\dfrac{\pi}{2} \).

Answer   \( -8i \)

q: Evaluate \( \left(\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}\right)^{10} \) using De Moivre's theorem.
c:
Solution

\[1+i=\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\]

\[1-i=\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)\]

\[\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}=\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}=i\]

\[\left(\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}\right)^{10}=i^{10}=(i^2)^5=-1\]


Answer   \( -1 \)

q: Evaluate \( (\sqrt{3} + i)^5 \) using De Moivre's theorem, in the form \( x + yi \).
c:
Solution

\[\sqrt{3}+i=2\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\]

\[\begin{aligned}(\sqrt{3}+i)^5&=2^5\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)\\&=32\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac12 i\right)\\&=-16\sqrt{3}+16i.\end{aligned}\]


Answer   \( -16\sqrt{3}+16i \)

q: Given \( z = 1 - i \), find \( z^{-1} \) using trigonometric form and check that \( z\, z^{-1} = 1 \).
c:
Solution

\[z=\sqrt{2}\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)\]

\[z^{-1}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)=\dfrac{1+i}{2}\]

Check: \( (1-i)\dfrac{1+i}{2}=\dfrac{1+1}{2}=1 \).

Answer   \( \dfrac{1+i}{2} \)

q: Find the square roots of the complex number \( z = -16 \).
c:
Solution

\[z=16(\cos\pi+i\sin\pi)\]

\[w_k=4\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi+2k\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi+2k\pi}{2}\right),\quad k=0,1\]

\[k=0:\quad w_0=4i\qquad k=1:\quad w_1=-4i\]


Answer   \( \pm 4i \)

q: Solve the equation \( z^3 = 64 \), where \( z \) is a complex number.
c:
Solution

\[64=64(\cos 0+i\sin 0)\]

\[z_k=4\left(\cos\dfrac{2k\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{2k\pi}{3}\right),\quad k=0,1,2\]

\[k=0:\quad z_0=4\]

\[k=1:\quad z_1=4\left(-\dfrac12+\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}i\right)=-2+2\sqrt{3}\, i\]

\[k=2:\quad z_2=-2-2\sqrt{3}\, i\]


Answer   \( 4,\; -2\pm 2\sqrt{3}\, i \)

q: Find the square roots of the complex number \( z = 8 - 8\sqrt{3}\, i \).
c:
Solution

\[r=\sqrt{64+192}=16\]

\[\cos\theta=\dfrac12,\quad\sin\theta=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\implies\theta=-\dfrac{\pi}{3}\]

\[w_k=4\left(\cos\dfrac{-\frac{\pi}{3}+2k\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{-\frac{\pi}{3}+2k\pi}{2}\right),\quad k=0,1\]

\[k=0:\quad w_0=4\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)=2\sqrt{3}-2i\]

\[k=1:\quad w_1=4\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right)=-2\sqrt{3}+2i\]


Answer   \( \pm(2\sqrt{3}-2i) \)

q: Solve the equation \( z^3 = -27i \), where \( z \) is a complex number.
c:
Solution

\[-27i=27\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)\]

\[z_k=3\left(\cos\dfrac{-\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{-\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{3}\right),\quad k=0,1,2\]

\[k=0:\quad z_0=3\left(\cos\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+i\sin\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac{3}{2}i\]

\[k=1:\quad z_1=3i\]

\[k=2:\quad z_2=3\left(\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)=-\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac{3}{2}i\]


Answer   \( \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac{3}{2}i,\; 3i,\; -\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}-\dfrac{3}{2}i \)

q: Find the cube roots of the complex number \( z = i \).
c:
Solution

\[i=\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2}\]

\[z_k=\cos\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{3}+i\sin\dfrac{\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi}{3},\quad k=0,1,2\]

\[k=0:\quad z_0=\cos\dfrac{\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac12 i\]

\[k=1:\quad z_1=\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{6}+i\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6}=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac12 i\]

\[k=2:\quad z_2=\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+i\sin\dfrac{3\pi}{2}=-i\]


Answer   \( \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac12 i,\; -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac12 i,\; -i \)
